articles.summary:

articles.title: TeamViewer Vulnerabilities Could Let Hackers Execute Malicious Code Through Remote Desktop Sessions
articles.summary:
TeamViewer has released security updates for three high-severity vulnerabilities that could let attackers run malicious code, crash remote desktop clients, or gain root access on macOS. The flaws affect client components used with TeamViewer Remote, TeamViewer Tensor, and TeamViewer ONE, with CVSS scores reaching 8.8. The company published security bulletin TV-2026-1011 on October 27, 2026, […]

articles.summary:

articles.title: OWASP Finds ChatGPT Helped Low-Skilled User Take Over Admin Account in Hacking Test
articles.summary:
OWASP found that ChatGPT helped an operator with no offensive security knowledge take over an administrator account during a controlled hacking test. The operator largely copied commands, returned results to the chatbot, and followed its guidance to change a password and log in. The finding shows how AI can lower the skill needed for some […]

articles.title: Google Fixes 52 Chrome Security Flaws, Including Four Critical Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Google released a Chrome security update that fixes 52 vulnerabilities, including four critical flaws affecting FileSystem, FileAPI, Skia, and Layout. According to the release notice, the Stable channel is moving to version 156.0.8078.73/.74 for Windows and Mac. At the same time, Linux users will receive version 156.0.8078.73. articles.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Bulletproof Hosting Domain Linked to Ransomware and Cybercrime
articles.summary:
The FBI seized virtualine.net, the main website of a bulletproof hosting provider linked to ransomware operators, stolen-data markets, and other cybercrime services. Announced on October 27, 2026, the court-authorized action targeted a business accused of helping criminals keep their websites online, ignore abuse complaints, and hide payments. articles.title: Malicious Firefox Extensions Impersonate Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget to Steal Crypto Wallet Keys
articles.summary:
Three malicious Firefox extensions posed as the Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget crypto wallets to steal recovery phrases and private keys.
